summary: Sohini Sengupta is an Indologist who is a doctoral student at the University of Chicago, where she held a PhD student post in 2024.

Soiku Shigematsu (b. 1943) studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, University of Tokyo, Kyoto University, and under Kiju Shigematsu. He held posts at Shizuoka Women's University, Shizuoka University, Kansai Medical University, and was a Fulbright scholar in 1986.
Sojo Hirano (1928–2007) was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as an assistant professor at Hanazono University (attested 1974) and as a shike at Zuigan-ji (attested 1992–1996).
Sokatsu Shaku (1870–1954) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Kōsen Imakita and Soyen Shaku. He founded Ryobokai (1901), the Ryobokai Dojo of North America (1906), and Ningen Zen.

Sokei-an Shigetsu Sasaki (1882–1945) was a Buddhist studies teacher who studied at Tokyo Academy of Fine Arts, San Francisco Art Institute, and California Institute of the Arts, as well as under Sokatsu Shaku and Soyen Shaku, and founded the First Zen Institute of America (1930).

Sokichi Tsuda (1873–1961), active in history, archaeology, sinology, and Japanology, studied at Tōkyō Senmon Gakkō. He worked at the SMR Research Department (~1908–1914), taught at Waseda University (~1920–1940), and held a post at the University of Tokyo (~1923–1940).

Soko Morinaga (1925–1995) studied at Toyama High School and Daitoku-ji under Sesso Oda and Zuigan Goto. In Buddhist and religious studies, he served as head of Hanazono University (1986–1994) and abbot of Daishuin (~1963–1995).

Sokuo Eto (1888–1958) was a Buddhist studies scholar educated at Komazawa University, Kyoto University, and the University of Tokyo. He founded Dokenryo in 1937, served as president of Komazawa Junior College (~1950–1958), and was a professor at Komazawa University in 1953.

Solomon Caesar Malan (1812–1894) studied at St Edmund Hall, Oxford, and the University of Edinburgh. Working in Indology and linguistics, he was classical lecturer at Bishop's College, Calcutta, Secretary of The Asiatic Society, and a Fellow at Balliol College, Oxford.

Solomon George FitzHerbert earned his doctorate at the University of Oxford, working in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He served as Departmental Lecturer at Oxford and was a researcher at the National Centre for Scientific Research (attested 2019).
Soma Thera (1898–1960) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at St. Benedict's College, Colombo, and under Jetavana Sayadaw. He was also a member of Servants of the Buddha around 1929.

Somadeva Vasudeva is an Indologist who earned his PhD at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. He held posts at the French Institute of Pondicherry, Columbia University, Wolfson College, Oxford, and Kyoto University.

Somboon Watana is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who earned a PhD at Panjab University under Rekha Jhanji and Dharmanand Sharma. He serves as an Assistant Professor at Mahidol University (attested 2026).

Somchai Kusalacitto is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned a Ph.D. at the University of Madras and served as dean and deputy rector for foreign affairs at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2003).

Somdet Phra Nyanasamvara (1913–2013) studied at Wat Bowonniwet Vihara and under Vajirayanavangsa and Swami Satyananda Puri. In Buddhist studies, he was director at Mahamakut Buddhist University (1961), abbot of Wat Bowonniwet Vihara (~1961–2013), and taught meditation at Kasetsart University (1976).
Somphong Santacitto is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master's degree at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under the supervision of Phra Suthithammanuwat (attested 2006).

Somsak Phansiri, working in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics, earned a Doctor of Philosophy from the University of Madras (2005–2011) and served as a lecturer at Buriram Rajabhat University in 2026.

Sonam Chhoki, active in Tibetology, history, and archaeology, earned an M.A. at Jawaharlal Nehru University and a Ph.D. at SOAS University of London, and worked as a history teacher at Samtse College of Education.
Sonam Choden is a researcher in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Hamburg as a doctoral local researcher and worked there as a project employee (attested 2026).

Sonam Gyatso (b. 1933) is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who worked as a research assistant at Toyo Bunko and held a professorship at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2014).
